minutes.headline: Planning Board endorsed two ANRs and continued the 494 Electric Ave hearing to Feb 24, with a site visit set for Feb 19.
minutes.summary: The board endorsed two approval-not-required plans, heard that new state ADU rules strip local controls, and got a DCR briefing on mandatory flood map and bylaw updates. Most of the night went to the 494 Electric Avenue parking and retail hearing, where traffic safety and who owns Pierce Avenue stayed unresolved, so it was continued and a site visit was arranged. A storm water hearing for 213 Electric Avenue was continued, and the board discussed standard conditions, the stalled Master Plan committee, committee reports and minutes.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at start; none offered.
Supported the 494 Electric Ave project; urged agreeing on an entrance, a safe line of sight, and bringing the DPW engineer (Bill Bernard) and fire department to the site visit.
Urged the board to help existing businesses, questioned the need for a traffic study, and supported crosswalk signage and a turn lane.
Public comment on 213 Electric Ave storm water hearing; none offered.
Said conservation site walks are not public meetings and the board is on solid ground scheduling one.

budget_items.what_was_said: A remaining balance on the consultant contract was mentioned, with each consultant meeting costing roughly a stated amount; the contract term had reportedly already expired and continues informally.

budget_items.topic: Municipal Building Design Committee cost estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: A member relayed the presentation's renovation and new-build cost estimates and an overall total, noting omissions such as remediation.
Departments' cost estimates have sometimes been badly off, which affects committee votes.

budget_items.topic: Federal funds for the regional planning commission
budget_items.what_was_said: A federal funding freeze threatened regional planning projects and staff but was reportedly rescinded for now.
Chair noted the number of policies in the town and total coverage.
The 213 Electric Ave applicant paid for peer review in advance, which the board welcomed as saving town cost.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the 494 Electric Avenue hearing to February 24 after traffic safety and ownership of Pierce Avenue stayed unresolved.
A posted site visit at 494 Electric Avenue was set for Wednesday the 19th at 5:00 p.m., with DPW, police and fire invited.
The board voted to endorse two approval-not-required plans, for 215 Sunset Lane and 171 Arbor Street.
The 213 Electric Avenue storm water hearing was continued to March 10.
The planner was asked to draft a flood plain zoning amendment for DCR review ahead of the March 17 warrant deadline.

why_it_matters: The 494 Electric Avenue parking and retail project is not decided, and whether the town owns Pierce Avenue and how traffic enters the site are still open, so residents near it can still be heard at the site visit and the next hearing.
A flood plain bylaw amendment is required under the new flood maps and is headed for the warrant, so it is likely to be a vote residents are asked to take at Town Meeting.
watch_next: Site visit at 494 Electric Avenue on February 19, then the continued hearing on February 24.
The draft flood plain zoning amendment, due in about two weeks, ahead of the March 17 warrant deadline.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all four votes, the Master Plan contract figures, the flood plain zoning draft, the Pierce Avenue step and the 19 February site visit. The main difference is that our minutes record a deferral of a traffic peer review and a Board decision to invite DPW, police and fire to the site visit. The official minutes record neither as a Board decision.
